title: Multan, 1818
hookLine: the city of saints and heat joins the kingdom

cards: Heat that hits like an open oven door. Dust in the air, the sun white overhead, and rising out of the haze, the domes of shrines, glazed in blue and white tiles. Multan, far down in the south of the Punjab.
Some call it a city of saints, for its Sufi shrines, and a city of heat, for reasons you can feel on your skin. It has a fort, and a governor inside it who has no intention of giving it up.

teach.h: A BOWL OF MILK, FULL TO THE BRIM.
teach.b: Start long before the kingdom. Sikh tradition remembers Guru Nanak coming to Multan on his travels, and the janamsakhis, the old stories of his life, tell it this way.

The holy men of the city, hearing a new teacher had arrived, sent him a bowl of milk filled to the brim. The message was polite and clear: this city is already full of saints; there's no room for one more.
Guru Nanak laid a small jasmine flower on the milk. It floated, and not a drop spilled. His answer: I won't take your room; I'll only add a fragrance.
Now the siege. Ranjit Singh had tried for Multan before and been turned back. This time his army came to stay, with heavy guns, and the fort was surrounded through the heat.

teach.h: A GOVERNOR WHO FOUGHT TO THE END.
teach.b: Its governor, Nawab Muzaffar Khan, refused to surrender. Tradition says that when the walls were finally breached, he came out sword in hand with his sons beside him and fought until he fell.
Sikh accounts remember his courage with respect. An enemy can be honored.
Then Multan, with its shrines, its markets and its long road to the south, became part of the kingdom, which now reached deep into the south of the Punjab.
Put the two stories side by side: a flower that doesn't spill the milk, and a governor who wouldn't yield.
Multan joins, but the city of saints stays a city of saints.

how: Sikhs tell the janamsakhi story of Guru Nanak's jasmine flower on the bowl of milk at Multan, and Sikh histories remember the siege of Multan and the courage of its governor, Nawab Muzaffar Khan.

games.q: you're Guru Nanak at Multan. the city's holy men send you a bowl of milk filled to the brim: no room here. what do you do?
o: lay a small flower on the milk.
pour some out to make room.
games.why: the janamsakhis say he laid a jasmine flower on the milk and not a drop spilled: I won't take your room, I'll only add a fragrance.

practice: Let your mind travel to the hottest place you've ever stood, a summer street, a kitchen in July, a beach at noon, and feel the heat, the light pressing on your eyelids, the slowness it brings.
Then let a small cool thing arrive, a breeze, a cup of water, a white flower floating on milk, and let your breath slow around it, with Waheguru if you pray.

wordCard.voice: Multan. The city of saints and heat, where Guru Nanak laid a flower on the milk, and which joined Ranjit Singh's kingdom after a hard siege. Today's word.
